newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE announces key changes to white sugar contract.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE announces key changes to white sugar contract.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) announced significant changes to its No.5 white sugar contract with effect from the August 1998 delivery month.
A statement said on Friday that LIFFE reduced the maximum ICUMSA colour for non-EU ports for delivery against the contract from 60 units to 45.
It also increased the minimum loading rate for sugars delivered in fulfilment of delivery obligations from 750 tonnes to 1,000 tonnes a day.
Allowance is to made for delivery of sugar packed in polypropylene (PP) bags at a differential to be determined periodically by the LIFFE Board.
As from the August 1998 delivery month, the differential to the price payable for one lot of sugar packed in PP rather than in jute bags would be a discount of $6 per tonne, it said.

"The purpose of the amendments to LIFFE's No.5 white sugar futures contract is to ensure that the contract specifiations remain closely in line with current commercial practice in the underlying sugar market," said LIFFE Chief Executive Daniel Hodson in the statement.

"LIFFE's No.5 white sugar futures contract is the most widely traded white sugar futures contract in the world, and these changes will guarantee that the contract remains an effective risk management tool for the international sugar trade and industry."
Hodson said listing of the August 1998 delivery month and options expiry were delayed in January 1997 in order for the contract amendments to be effected, but these would now be listed on April 16.
LIFFE also made other clarifications to contract terms and administrative procedures.
These included clarification that the colour of sugar delivered from EU ports must be ICUMSA 45 or better.
It also removed the stipulation that that freight differentials should be set in reference to prevailing freight rates for vessels of 15 years of age or less.
